The book describes intersex conditions, hormone-related development, gender identity, sexual orientation, and differences in sexual expression."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"These sections should be read as distinct questions rather than merged into one explanation. Track which evidence concerns anatomy, genes, prenatal influences, behavior, or identity and note variation within each topic."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m10-2-study-1","text":"Variation is central, not an exception"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sex-related anatomy, gender-related behavior, identity, and sexual orientation are different dimensions that should not be treated as interchangeable. The module examines biological development through conditions in which chromosomes, hormones, anatomy, or receptor responses do not follow the most common combinations. Intersex variations provide evidence about the roles of prenatal development and endocrine mechanisms, but any particular individual's experience remains more complex than one biological variable."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m10-2-study-2","text":"What developmental conditions teach"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Congenital adrenal hyperplasia and androgen insensitivity are examples of circumstances that help researchers understand how hormone exposure and sensitivity relate to development. Outcomes are variable, and it is important not to infer identity from anatomy or to use clinical cases as simplistic experiments. Questions about sex assignment and upbringing have medical, ethical, and personal dimensions. A science-based answer should identify the actual biological mechanism and the limits of what a case demonstrates."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m10-2-study-3","text":"Sexual orientation and its influences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have investigated genetic patterns, prenatal influences, behavior, and neuroanatomy in relation to sexual orientation. No single factor offers a complete, deterministic account of an individual's orientation. Group-level findings do not constitute reliable tests of personal identity. Evolutionary questions about variation are research questions, not grounds for pathologizing or ranking people. Avoid equating correlation in one biological measure with proof of cause."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m10-2-study-4","text":"Gender identity and interpretation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Gender identity and gender-differentiated behaviors are studied across biological and developmental contexts. Transgender experiences cannot be reduced to a simple hormone test or one neural region. The module's recurring lesson is that human variation does not fit neatly into one dimension, and explanatory claims should preserve differences among anatomy, development, behavior, identity, and orientation. This is both scientifically more accurate and more respectful of individuals."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m10-2-h01","text":"Gender Identity and Gender-Differentiated .","sourcePrintedPage":341,"sourcePdfPage":359,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the point is that it was a mistake to impose surgery and hormonal .","sourcePrintedPage":342,"sourcePdfPage":360,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Surveys report that about 3.5 percent of adults in the United States identify as males.","headingId":"bp14-m10-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":342,"sourcePdfPage":360},{"type":"bullet","text":"A surgically created or lengthened vagina provides no sensation and requires frequent attention to prevent it from scarring over.","headingId":"bp14-m10-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":342,"sourcePdfPage":360},{"type":"bullet","text":"Physicians have no clear consensus on whether surgery to “correct” the genital appearance should occur early, late, or not at all.","headingId":"bp14-m10-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":342,"sourcePdfPage":360},{"type":"bullet","text":"Contrary to what occur in others .","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":60},{"text":"They choose their actions, but they do not choose their desires or orientation, any more than people choose to be left-handed or right-handed.","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":61},{"text":"Whereas most men discover their sexual orientation early, many women are slower.","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":62},{"text":"Boys’ femininetype behaviors in childhood and adolescence correlate strongly with same-sex orientation in adulthood , but girls’ masculine-type behaviors are relatively weak predictors of sexual orientation .","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":63},{"text":"Surveys report that about 3.5 percent of adults in the United States identify as gay or lesbian .","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":64},{"text":"The percentage also varies among countries, although we do not know how much of the apparent difference is due to secrecy or inaccurate reporting.","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":65},{"text":"Even though a man may have had both same-sex and opposite-sex experiences, his preference and fantasies almost always lean strongly one way more than the other, and few men change their orientation .","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":66},{"text":"Contrary to what biologists and others once assumed, same-sex genital contact occurs in nature for many animal species, and not just in those that cannot find a member of the opposite sex, or those with hormonal abnormalities.","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":137},{"text":"Frans de Waal (2022), who spent his career observing primates, described all bonobos as “bisexual.” If “natural” means “occurs in nature,” then same-sex activity is natural.","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":138}],"originalFacts":7,"additionalFacts":2,"glossary":[{"term":"Primates","definition":"order the face, sound of the voice, and ratio of the index finger to the ring finger .","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":68},{"text":"However, let’s emphasize the terms “slightly” and “on average.” The difference in height is on average only half an inch (1.5 cm).","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":69},{"text":"People who differ in sexual orientation also tend to differ in many behaviors not directly connected to sex.","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":70},{"text":"Gay men are more likely than average to choose female-typical careers such as florist or hair stylist .","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":71},{"text":"Also, whereas heterosexual men usually give directions in terms of distances and north, south, east, or west, women and gay men are more likely to describe landmarks .","printedPage":342,"pdfPage":360,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":72}],"originalFacts":5,"additionalFacts":0,"glossary":[],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":142,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":117},{"id":"bp14-m10-2-h09","title":"Genetics","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m10-2-h07","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"facts":[{"text":"Early studies of the genetics of human sexual orientation began by advertising in gay or lesbian publications for readers of those magazines who had twins.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":74},{"text":"When someone responded, the researchers contacted the other twin to fill out a survey with miscellaneous questions that included sexual orientation.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":75},{"text":"However, the kind of person who answers an ad in a gay or lesbian magazine is not representative of all others.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":76},{"text":"A later study examined the data from all the twins in Sweden between ages 20 and 47 .","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":77},{"text":"The Swedish study differed not only in the breadth of the sample but also in the behavioral criterion.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"Instead of asking about sexual orientation, the researchers asked whether someone had ever had a same-sex partner.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"In short, the results indicate some heritability of sexual orientation, but the size of the effect is uncertain, and the mechanism is also uncertain.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":80},{"text":"Note, this does not say that monozygotic twins are more likely to have a same-sex orientation than dizygotic twins are.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":139},{"text":"It says that monozygotic twins are more likely to have the same sexual orientation.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":140}],"originalFacts":7,"additionalFacts":2,"glossary":[{"term":"Monozygotic twins","definition":"twins derived from one egg","sourcePrintedPage":627,"sourcePdfPage":645},{"term":"Dizygotic twins","definition":"fraternal (non-identical) twins derived from two eggs","sourcePrintedPage":622,"sourcePdfPage":640},{"term":"Heritability","definition":"estimate of the degree to which variation in a characteristic depends on genetic variations in a given man.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":82},{"text":"That is, those who do not have children themselves might do a better than average job of helping their siblings rear children.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":83},{"text":"Survey data in the United States indicate that gay men are no more likely, and perhaps less likely, than heterosexuals to support their relatives .","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":84},{"text":"However, observations in Samoa found that gay men are more helpful than average toward their nephews and nieces, in ways such as baby-sitting, tutoring, or contributing money .","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":85},{"text":"It is difficult to know what might have been the usual pattern through human existence.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":86},{"text":"Researchers identified genes that were more common than average among people who had at least one same-sex encounter.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":87},{"text":"The genes that the researchers found may reflect openness to new experiences, or willingness to take risks, or just a strong sex drive, rather than samesex attraction .","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":88},{"text":"A second idea is that sexual orientation relates to epigenetics rather than changes in DNA sequence.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":141},{"text":"It is possible for environmental events to attach an acetyl group or a methyl group (CH 3 ) to activate or inactivate a gene.","printedPage":343,"pdfPage":361,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":142}],"originalFacts":7,"additionalFacts":2,"glossary":[{"term":"Epigenetics","definition":"a of brain development .","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":90},{"text":"Animal studies have shown that prenatal or early postnatal hormones produce organizing effects on both external anatomy and brain development, but the external anatomy develops earlier than the brain.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":91},{"text":"Therefore, it is possible for hormones to alter the brain without changing external anatomy.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":92},{"text":"Researchers tested mothers of gay sons with older brothers and found elevated levels of antibodies against a protein produced by the Y chromosome .","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":93},{"text":"The sons, however, despite normal male anatomy, often responded to the presence of another male by arching their backs in the typical rat female posture for sex .","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":94},{"text":"Males that were subjected to both stress and alcohol in prenatal development had decreased male sexual behaviors as well as the increased female behaviors .","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":95},{"text":"The long-term effects of either prenatal stress or alcohol include several changes in the structure of the nervous system .","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":96},{"text":"However, these studies relied on women’s memories of pregnancies more than 20 years earlier.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":97},{"text":"In short, researchers have identified several possible biological influences on sexual orientation, but much remains unknown.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":98},{"text":"On average, gay and heterosexual men have nearly the same hormone levels, and most lesbian women have about the same hormone levels as heterosexual women.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":143},{"text":"Research has shown that prenatal stress alters sexual development in laboratory animals.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":144},{"text":"Although these studies pertained to rats, they prompted investigators to examine possible effects of prenatal stress on humans.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":145},{"text":"In two of the three, the mothers of sons with a same-sex orientation recalled more than average stressful experiences.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":146}],"originalFacts":9,"additionalFacts":4,"glossary":[{"term":"Organizing partly in the female-typical direction for a few structures.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":100},{"text":"The most widely cited research concerns the third interstitial nucleus of the anterior hypothalamus (INAH-3), which is generally more than twice as large in heterosexual men as in women.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":101},{"text":"This area has more cells with androgen receptors in men than in women , and it probably plays a role in male sexual behavior, although the exact role is uncertain.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":102},{"text":"In other species it is known as the sexually dimorphic nucleus , although calling it a “nucleus” is a bit of an overstatement.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":103},{"text":"Researchers found that the INAH-3 nucleus of women.","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":104},{"text":"On microscopic examination of the INAH-3, researchers found that heterosexual men had larger neurons than homosexual men but about the same number.","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":105},{"text":"To interpret these results, we need to ask whether neurons.","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":106},{"text":"Some neurons do grow or shrink in adults because of hormones or behavioral activities .","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":107},{"text":"Similarly, the brains of lesbians resemble those of heterosexual women in most ways, but they are shifted in the male direction in a few ways.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":147},{"text":"Simon LeVay (1991) examined INAH-3 in 41 people who had died between the ages of 26 and 59.","printedPage":344,"pdfPage":362,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":148},{"text":"Le- Vay (1993) later AIDS.","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":149},{"text":"If you could examine a man’s INAH-3, you could make a reasonable guess about sexual orientation, but you could not be confident.","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":150},{"text":"(Whether this area corresponds to human INAH-3 is uncertain.) This area becomes larger in male than female sheep before birth as a result of prenatal testosterone levels.","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":151},{"text":"In sheep, at least, an anatomical difference appears result.","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":152}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":6,"glossary":[{"term":"Sexually .","printedPage":345,"pdfPage":363,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":112},{"text":"When someone reaches adolescence and requests a gender change, the insanity.","printedPage":346,"pdfPage":364,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":155},{"text":"In most cases, people who have both requested and development.","printedPage":347,"pdfPage":365,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":157},{"text":"Another possibility is that intersexuality may be Troops of monkeys or chimpanzees demonstrate different expectations for males and females, and in those cases it is reasonable to talk about gender, as well as gender nonconforming behavior.","Most people accept the gender identity that matches their external appearance, but some do not.","At one time, psychologists assumed that gender identity and related behaviors depended almost entirely how parents rear their children. However, several kinds of evidence suggest that prenatal hormones are important also.","A genetic male with low levels of testosterone or testosterone receptors may develop a female or intermediate appearance.","A genetic female who is exposed to more testosterone than the average female can be partly masculinized.","The most common cause of an intermediate sexual anatomy is congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), meaning overdevelopment of the adrenal glands. The pituitary secretes adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), which stimulates the adrenal gland to release cortisol and other hormones, and cortisol feeds back to decrease ACTH.","If a fetus has a genetic limitation in the ability to produce cortisol, the pituitary fails to receive the usual feedback signal, and it continues secreting more ACTH, stimulating the adrenal gland beyond the usual level.","The accuracy of these estimates is uncertain, as hospitals and families keep the information private. Confidentiality is important, but an unfortunate consequence is that intersex people have trouble finding others like themselves.","However, their brains were exposed to elevated testosterone levels during prenatal and early postnatal life.","As discussed in the first module of this chapter, prenatal levels of testosterone correlate with girls’ toy choices.","The girls with CAH played with boys’ toys more than most other girls did, but less than the average for boys. The girls exposed to the largest amount of testosterone in early development showed the largest preference for boys’ toys.","Observations found that the parents generally encouraged the girls to play with whatever they wanted to play with.","Another difference is that on average, girls with CAH also perform slightly better than most other girls on spatial and mechanical skills.","When the girls who had CAH reach adolescence, their interests tend to be intermediate between those of typical males and females. Compared to other girls, they tend to read more sports magazines and fewer style and glamour magazines.","If someone with an XY chromosome pattern has a deficiency in the receptor for androgens, circulating androgens have little or no effect.","This condition, known as androgen insensitivity or testicular feminization, produces an anatomy ranging from a smaller than average penis to an external appearance of a typical female, in which case no one has any reason to suspect the person is anything other than female, until puberty. Then, although the breasts develop and hips broaden, menstruation does not occur, because the body has undescended testes instead of ovaries and a uterus.","Also, pubic hair is sparse or absent, because it depends on androgens in females as well as males.","To resolve the roles of rearing and hormones in determining gender identity, the most decisive observation would come from rearing a normal male baby as a female or rearing a normal female baby as a male.","If the resulting adult fully accepts the assigned role, we would know that upbringing determines gender identity.","Although no one would perform such an experiment intentionally, we can learn from accidental events. In some cases, someone was exposed to a more-or-less normal pattern of male hormones in early development but then reared as a girl.","The girl-turned-boy developed a male gender identity and directed his sexual interest toward females.","Later results from 44 countries found that many but not all such people changed their identity from female to male during adolescence, with percentages that vary across countries.","However, the point is that it was a mistake to impose surgery and hormonal treatments to try to force this child to become female. When the prenatal hormone pattern of the brain conflicts with a child’s appearance, no one can be sure how that child will develop psychologically.","Girls with CAH and related conditions are born with appearances ranging from almost typical female to a partly masculinized external appearance.","Some genetic males are born with a very small penis because of a condition called cloacal exstrophy, a defect of pelvis development.","Despite their genital anatomy, they had typical male levels of testosterone in prenatal development.","genitals should be reared as a girl, using surgery if necessary to make the genitals look more feminine. The reason was that surgery to approximate female appearance is easier than surgery to approximate male appearance.","Physicians and psychologists assumed that if a child looks like a girl and the parents rear her as a girl, she will fully accept that identity.","Girls with the CAH history have a difficult sexual adjustment, especially if they were subjected to clitorisreduction surgery to make them look more female. Most are reared as girls, and most are reasonably satisfied with this designation, although some consider themselves gender-fluid and many are either lesbian or bisexual.","Rearing a CAH genetic female as male has disadvantages, including the need to surgically remove the ovaries before puberty to prevent breast growth and other female-typical developments.","Exclusive, lifelong same-sex orientation has so far been observed only in humans and sheep, although it may occur in others.","They choose their actions, but they do not choose their desires or orientation, any more than people choose to be left-handed or right-handed.","Whereas most men discover their sexual orientation early, many women are slower. Boys’ femininetype behaviors in childhood and adolescence correlate strongly with same-sex orientation in adulthood, but girls’ masculine-type behaviors are relatively weak predictors of sexual orientation.","Surveys report that about 3.5 percent of adults in the United States identify as gay or lesbian.","The percentage also varies among countries, although we do not know how much of the apparent difference is due to secrecy or inaccurate reporting. Even though a man may have had both same-sex and opposite-sex experiences, his preference and fantasies almost always lean strongly one way more than the other, and few men change their orientation.","Gay men and heterosexual men differ slightly on average in height, weight, shape of the face, sound of the voice, and ratio of the index finger to the ring finger.","However, let’s emphasize the terms “slightly” and “on average.” The difference in height is on average only half an inch (1.5 cm).","People who differ in sexual orientation also tend to differ in many behaviors not directly connected to sex. Gay men are more likely than average to choose female-typical careers such as florist or hair stylist.","Also, whereas heterosexual men usually give directions in terms of distances and north, south, east, or west, women and gay men are more likely to describe landmarks.","Early studies of the genetics of human sexual orientation began by advertising in gay or lesbian publications for readers of those magazines who had twins.","When someone responded, the researchers contacted the other twin to fill out a survey with miscellaneous questions that included sexual orientation.","However, the kind of person who answers an ad in a gay or lesbian magazine is not representative of all others. A later study examined the data from all the twins in Sweden between ages 20 and 47.","The Swedish study differed not only in the breadth of the sample but also in the behavioral criterion.","Instead of asking about sexual orientation, the researchers asked whether someone had ever had a same-sex partner. In short, the results indicate some heritability of sexual orientation, but the size of the effect is uncertain, and the mechanism is also uncertain.","On average, a gay man has about one-fifth as many children as a heterosexual man.","That is, those who do not have children themselves might do a better than average job of helping their siblings rear children.","Survey data in the United States indicate that gay men are no more likely, and perhaps less likely, than heterosexuals to support their relatives. However, observations in Samoa found that gay men are more helpful than average toward their nephews and nieces, in ways such as baby-sitting, tutoring, or contributing money.","It is difficult to know what might have been the usual pattern through human existence.","Researchers identified genes that were more common than average among people who had at least one same-sex encounter. The genes that the researchers found may reflect openness to new experiences, or willingness to take risks, or just a strong sex drive, rather than samesex attraction.","However, it is possible that sexual orientation depends on hormone levels during a sensitive period of brain development.","Animal studies have shown that prenatal or early postnatal hormones produce organizing effects on both external anatomy and brain development, but the external anatomy develops earlier than the brain.","Therefore, it is possible for hormones to alter the brain without changing external anatomy.","Researchers tested mothers of gay sons with older brothers and found elevated levels of antibodies against a protein produced by the Y chromosome. The sons, however, despite normal male anatomy, often responded to the presence of another male by arching their backs in the typical rat female posture for sex.","Males that were subjected to both stress and alcohol in prenatal development had decreased male sexual behaviors as well as the increased female behaviors.","The long-term effects of either prenatal stress or alcohol include several changes in the structure of the nervous system. However, these studies relied on women’s memories of pregnancies more than 20 years earlier.","In short, researchers have identified several possible biological influences on sexual orientation, but much remains unknown.","On average, the brains of gay men resemble those of heterosexual men in most ways, but they are shifted partly in the female-typical direction for a few structures.","The most widely cited research concerns the third interstitial nucleus of the anterior hypothalamus (INAH-3), which is generally more than twice as large in heterosexual men as in women.","This area has more cells with androgen receptors in men than in women, and it probably plays a role in male sexual behavior, although the exact role is uncertain. In other species it is known as the sexually dimorphic nucleus, although calling it a “nucleus” is a bit of an overstatement.","Researchers found that the INAH-3 nucleus of homosexual men was intermediate between those of heterosexual men and heterosexual women.","On microscopic examination of the INAH-3, researchers found that heterosexual men had larger neurons than homosexual men but about the same number.","To interpret these results, we need to ask whether differences in the hypothalamus influence sexual orientation, or sexual activity influences the size of hypothalamic neurons. Some neurons do grow or shrink in adults because of hormones or behavioral activities.","Transgender people are those who affirm that they were “born in the wrong body,” that although their anatomy appears male or female, they clearly identify with the other gender.","Estimates of the prevalence of transgender people in the United States range from 0.3 to 0.6 percent, but these may be underestimates, because many transgender people prefer to avoid public identification.","Transgender people have some interests and activities that are not typical of their birth sex, but most people with genderatypical interests or activities do not identify as transgender. Some aspects of brain anatomy of transgender people resemble others of their birth sex, some aspects resemble those of their experienced gender, and some are intermediate.","When someone reaches adolescence and requests a gender change, the recommendation is as follows: It is unwise to make irreversible physical changes at once, because many children who say they want to be the opposite sex change their mind during the","People today are more aware and generally more accepting of sexual diversity than they were in Kinsey’s time.","Biological research will not tell us how to treat one another, but it can help us understand how we come to be different.","Puberty-blocking drugs (to prevent body changes corresponding to the original, rejected sex) can be given to children at least 12 years old who have intense distress about their assigned gender.","It is important to get informed consent, which can be tricky for 12-year-olds, and some have regretted their decision later. At age 16, if the adolescent still wishes to proceed, treatment can start with hormones of the desired sex.","On average, intersexes have IQ scores in the 110 to 125 range, well above the mean for the population."],"classroomResearch":{"title":"Evidence in context: Discrepancies of Sexual Appearance","body":"Although no one would perform such an experiment intentionally, we can learn from accidental events.","printedPages":[340],"pdfPages":[358],"kind":"textbook_selected_research","evidenceMethod":"single_verified_textbook_passage"},"classroomCoverage":{"status":"source_structured_full_book","level":"comprehensive_book_derived","topicHeadings":14,"bullets":46,"newWords":2145,"allTopicsWithExplanations":true,"sourceScope":"verified_pdf_topic_facts_crosschecked_with_uploaded_markdown"}},{"id":"bp14-m11-1","chapterId":"bp14-ch11","moduleId":"bp14-m11-1","moduleNumber":"11.1","title":"What Is Emotion?","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":352,"printedEnd":362,"pdfStart":370,"pdfEnd":380,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Emotion includes bodily responses, brain activity, expression, and patterns of action. Researchers disagree about how best to define and categorize emotions, including whether to treat them as basic categories or continuous dimensions."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module considers autonomic arousal, hemispheric differences, and the functions of emotions in judgment and behavior. Notice how physiological responses and interpretations influence one another."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m11-1-study-1","text":"Emotion has several components"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An emotional episode can involve subjective feeling, bodily arousal, attention, action tendencies, and expression. These components influence one another but need not always match perfectly. A person may show physiological activation without identifying a clear emotion, or may describe a strong feeling without large changes in every bodily measure. The question of what emotion is cannot be answered by observing heart rate alone. Study emotion as a coordinated but flexible response to events that matter to the organism."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m11-1-study-2","text":"Arousal, interpretation, and feedback"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Autonomic changes can prepare the body for action and influence how an experience feels. Research asks whether bodily arousal is necessary for emotion, how interpretation changes emotional experience, and whether actions can alter feelings. Facial expressions and patterns of behavior may contribute feedback, but the effect is neither absolute nor the same in every situation. The important distinction is between a bodily response, a conscious emotional label, and the behavior that follows."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m11-1-study-3","text":"How the brain represents emotion"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Networks including cortical and subcortical regions contribute to detecting significance, remembering context, preparing responses, and regulating behavior. Hemispheric differences have been studied, but emotions are not stored exclusively in one hemisphere. Researchers debate whether emotions are best classified as a few basic categories or described along continuous dimensions such as valence and arousal. Both approaches may help at different levels, provided they are tied to observations rather than assumed as definitions."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m11-1-study-4","text":"Emotion and decisions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Emotions influence which events receive attention, which goals seem urgent, and how people weigh consequences. They can support adaptive action but can also bias moral judgment or choice. The module's most useful conclusion is that feeling, physiology, expression, and cognitive evaluation are interrelated processes. Any claim that 'the emotional brain' simply overrides 'the rational brain' is too crude to explain their cooperation."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h01","text":"Emotion and Autonomic Arousal"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers had long recognized that the sympathetic nervous system stimulates certain organs, such as the heart, while inhibiting others, such as the stomach and intestines.","sourcePrintedPage":352,"sourcePdfPage":370,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Walter Cannon was the first to recognize the pattern: It stimulates organs important for vigorous “fight-or-flight” activities while inhibiting vegetative activities that can wait until later.","sourcePrintedPage":352,"sourcePdfPage":370,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The parasympathetic nervous system is the “rest and digest” system that saves energy and prepares for later needs.","sourcePrintedPage":352,"sourcePdfPage":370,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If a small animal sees a potential predator at a great distance, it becomes alert, but motionless. (The predator is less likely to notice an immobile animal.) The little animal’s heart rate decreases , by increased parasympathetic input.","sourcePrintedPage":352,"sourcePdfPage":370,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h02","text":"Is Physiological Arousal Necessary for Emotion?"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In people with a condition called pure autonomic failure , the autonomic nervous system completely or almost completely ceases activity.","sourcePrintedPage":353,"sourcePdfPage":371,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The heart and other organs continue to function, but the nervous system no longer regulates them.","sourcePrintedPage":353,"sourcePdfPage":371,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They report “having” the same emotions as anyone else, and they have little difficulty identifying what emotion a character in a story would probably experience , but they feel their emotions less intensely than before .","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Presumably, when they report experiencing emotions, they refer mainly to the cognitive aspect: “I’m angry, because this is a situation that calls for anger.” People with damage to the right somatosensory cortex have typical autonomic responses to emotional music but report little subjective experience.","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h03","text":"Actions Alter Emotions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It is easier to feel angry while standing (and therefore in a position to attack) than while lying in a more helpless position .","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because perceptions of your body’s actions contribute to your emotional feelings, psychologists describe emotions as “embodied”—that is, they depend on the body’s responses.","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers could not test this hypothesis simply by telling people to smile or frown and then asking how they felt.","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To disguise their intention, they asked people to hold a pen with either the teeth or the lips.","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The first study reported that people holding a pen with their teeth were more likely to rate cartoons as being funny .","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When people face a camera, they tend to think about how they look on the camera, and it changes their reactions.","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A later study found that holding the pen in the teeth did increase amusement if no camera was","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Laboratory studies have found support for the facial feedback hypothesis that is reasonably dependable, although it is a small effect .","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another way to alter facial expressions is to use botulinum toxin (Botox), which blocks transmission at nerve– muscle junctions.","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h04","text":"Basic Emotions or Continuous Dimensions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In the late 1800s and early 1900s, psychological researchers hoped to identify the elements of the mind, analogous to the elements of chemistry.","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They debated whether the psychological elements were thoughts, ideas, images, or something else.","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Later psychologists hoped to find the elements of motivation, offering lists of the basic motivations.","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That pursuit led to such fascinating questions as whether breathing counts as just one motivation or two (inhaling and exhaling).","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Today, emotion is the only area in which many researchers still hope to identify the elements, the “basic” emotions.","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The alternative is to regard emotional experience in terms of continuous dimensions.","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h05","text":"Brain Representations of Emotion"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heart rate and breathing rate increase with the intensity of an emotion, but they do not distinguish fear from anger, or any other pair of emotions.","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditionally, the limbic system — the forebrain areas surrounding the thalamus—has been regarded as important for emotion (Figure 11.3).","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have used PET or fMRI techniques to identify brain areas that respond while people look at emotional pictures or listen to emotional stories.","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The only emotion that seems to depend mostly on one brain area is disgust, which exhibits a link to the insula, a cortical area that is also important for taste .","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The researchers described the third gradient as “complexity,” ranging from conflict at one pole to unambiguous emotion (usually fearful) at the other .","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In short, these findings support the idea that brain responses are well described as dimensions of emotion rather than as discrete categories .","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h06","text":"Hemispheric Differences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Activity of the left hemisphere, especially its frontal and temporal lobes, relates to what Jeffrey Gray","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"called the behavioral activation system (BAS) , marked by low to moderate autonomic arousal and a tendency to approach, which could characterize happiness or anger.","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Activity of right hemisphere, again mainly the frontal and temporal lobes, is associated with the behavioral inhibition system (BIS) .","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The BIS was initially described as responsible for withdrawal, but according to later research it is better described as inhibiting impulses and resolving conflict between drives .","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with greater right-hemisphere activity tend to be more socially withdrawn, cautious, and prone to unpleasant emotions .","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h07","text":"Expressing Emotion"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The main support for the idea of basic emotions has relied on consistency of facial expressions.","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People who are blind since birth exhibit expressions of happiness, sadness, fear, pride, and shame that resemble those of sighted people .","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It is agreed that some emotional expressions are partly built-in, though capable of learned modification.","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The controversial issue is whether those expressions fall into a small number of discrete categories.","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If presented with a set of faces, such as those in Figure 11.6, and given a list of emotion terms, most people in cultures throughout the world pair them up with greater-than-chance accuracy.","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The procedure of asking people to match the six faces to six labels exaggerates the accuracy.","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The procedure requires use of those six labels, even if an observer would have used some other label.","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Finally, even if it were true that people could identify six emotions from facial expressions, that evidence would not demonstrate that we have precisely six emotions.","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Previous research had found disruptions in that axon tract in several psychiatric conditions marked by poor social relationships.","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In short, details of brain anatomy have much to do with the ability to recognize emotional expressions.","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h08","text":"The Functions of Emotion"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If we evolved the capacity to experience and express emotions, emotions must have served some adaptive function.","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Disgust tells us to avoid something that might cause illness.","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The adaptive value of happiness, sadness, embarrassment, and other emotions is more speculative, although psychologists have suggested plausible possibilities.","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research has also found that emotions provide a useful guide when we need to make a quick decision.","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h09","text":"Emotions and Moral Decisions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When we make important decisions, we pay much attention to how we think an outcome will make us feel.","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, although that may be true logically, the decisions","sourcePrintedPage":359,"sourcePdfPage":377,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain scans demonstrate that contemplating these dilemmas activates brain areas known to respond to emotions, including parts of the prefrontal cortex and cingulate gyrus .","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with the strongest autonomic arousal are the least likely to decide to kill one to save five others .","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with such damage tend to make decisions without much consideration of the emotional impact .","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When confronted with the moral dilemmas we just discussed, they are more likely than average to choose the utilitarian option of killing one to save five .","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Almost everyone shudders and says of course not, but some people with damage to the ventromedial prefrontal cortex calmly say it would be okay to do so .","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m11-1-h10","text":"In Closing: Emotions and the Nervous System"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Biological research sheds light on important questions about the psychology of emotions.","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, it supports the idea of that emotions occur along dimensions instead of distinct categories.","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain damage studies suggest that emotional reactions are often a useful quick guide to appropriate moral actions.","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some people with ventromedial prefrontal cortex damage say yes, especially if the damage occurred early in life .","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During the next few months, he exhibited impulsive behavior and poor decision making, two common symptoms of prefrontal damage.","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Any choice requires consideration of values and emotions—how we think one outcome or another will make us feel.","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In Damasio’s words, “Inevitably, emotions are inseparable from the idea of good and evil” .","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Emotional situations arouse both the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":352,"sourcePdfPage":370},{"type":"bullet","text":"Nearly all situations evoke a combination of sympathetic and parasympathetic arousal.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":352,"sourcePdfPage":370},{"type":"bullet","text":"We think of danger as something that would elicit mostly sympathetic activity, but often it does not.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":352,"sourcePdfPage":370},{"type":"bullet","text":"We humans also become alert and cautious and decrease our heart rate when we are aware of a possible danger at a distance.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":353,"sourcePdfPage":371},{"type":"bullet","text":"People with damage to part of the prefrontal cortex have weak autonomic responses but normal subjective responses.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372},{"type":"bullet","text":"These results suggest that autonomic responses and subjective experience are not always closely connected.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372},{"type":"bullet","text":"If you watch a horror movie in a cold room, where the temperature caused you to shiver, you might rate the movie as scarier than you would have in a warmer room.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372},{"type":"bullet","text":"According to the facial-feedback hypothesis, smiling may make you feel happier, and frowning may make you feel unhappier.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372},{"type":"bullet","text":"Similarly, getting people to sit up straight, by modifying the height of the chair and the desk, may also improve mood.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372},{"type":"bullet","text":"Getting people to frown by attaching golf tees to their eyebrows and telling them to keep touching the tips of the tees may increase unpleasant feelings.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":354,"sourcePdfPage":372},{"type":"bullet","text":"You could not identify anyone’s emotion by measuring autonomic a cortical area associated with happiness, sadness, disgust, fear, or anger.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373},{"type":"bullet","text":"The most salient point of this figure is the variability of locations for each emotion.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":355,"sourcePdfPage":373},{"type":"bullet","text":"On average, people with greater activity in the frontal cortex of the left hemisphere tend to be happier and more extraverted.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374},{"type":"bullet","text":"The hemispheres also differ in their contribution to perceiving others’ emotions.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374},{"type":"bullet","text":"In general, the right hemisphere is more active in perceiving emotions, especially negative emotions such as fear.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":356,"sourcePdfPage":374},{"type":"bullet","text":"The faces used in most research, including those in Figure 11.6, were posed to try to maximize recognition.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375},{"type":"bullet","text":"For spontaneous expressions, observers often perceive two or more emotions at a time, and observers’ guesses do not always match the self-reports by the people in the photographs.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another problem: People recognize expressions from their own culture better than those from other cultures.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375},{"type":"bullet","text":"Young people in two cultures largely isolated from Western influences were able to recognize the expression for happiness at better than 50 percent accuracy, but they had low accuracy on other expressions, especially the expression intended to depict anger.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":357,"sourcePdfPage":375},{"type":"bullet","text":"On average, young adults are better than older people in this regard, and women are better than men.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376},{"type":"bullet","text":"Researchers measured people’s ability to identify complex emotions from seeing just the eyes, as in Figure 11.8.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":358,"sourcePdfPage":376},{"type":"bullet","text":"In each of these dilemmas, you can save five people (including yourself in the lifeboat case) by killing one person.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h09","sourcePrintedPage":359,"sourcePdfPage":377},{"type":"bullet","text":"Most people say (hesitantly) that it is right to pull the switch in the trolley dilemma, fewer say yes in the footbridge and lifeboat dilemmas, and almost no one endorses killing one person to save five others in the hospital dilemma.","headingId":"bp14-m11-1-h09","sourcePrintedPage":360,"sourcePdfPage":378},{"type":"bullet","text":"When you make a moral decision, you compare the utilitarian aspect (for example, five
